newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money rises on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money rises on strong demand.

text.p: The Croatian interbank call money rate rose slightly on Friday and other rates remained firm due to very strong demand for kuna, dealers said.
"The situation is similar to Wednesday but banks' accounts have emptied further, so demand is much higher," one dealer said.
Corporate tax payment and some cash withdrawals ahead of the May 1 public holiday reduced the banking sector's overall balance to only 413 million kuna.
The central bank said it had 103 million in outstanding Lombard loans and expected the volume to rise this afternoon. It grants Lombard funds at 9.5 percent 12 days a month.
Money market trade is always more intense on Fridays as banks stock up their funds for the weekend after clients pay their weekly turnover tax.
Many lenders withdrew previous loans, the dealer said, and this caused as many as 17 banks to seek almost 70 million kuna this morning. Usually less than 10 banks seek funds.
"We have managed to settle 34.8 million so far (by 0900 GMT), but are still calling around for money," she added.
Most fresh trade was in call money funds at 10.5 percent, though some creditors charged 12 percent.
Three-day loans were granted at 11 percent and one-month at 15 percent, firmer again after some slight reductions by foreign banks earlier in the week.
